answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, with one stake-backed identity allowed per verified human or organization. Peers randomly audit completed work; proven fraud burns the stake and excludes the identity from future payouts. A fake-identity attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital for each Sybil, then risk losing it across all audited accounts. The umber ledger records each bond, while a ripple of correlated failures can trigger audits at the summit of high-value activity.
